uncertainties: The supplied material establishes normative propositions, not facts about any Product Provider's compliance. No conclusion of fulfilment follows from the source text alone.

Allocation of authority and responsibility, supervisory conduct, and operational or record-keeping outcomes require separate assessment. Governance and delegation terms could evidence retained authority; selection, monitoring and remediation records could evidence supervision; actual operational performance and ownership records could evidence outcomes. These are evidentiary categories, not an exhaustive checklist imposed by the excerpts.

Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 support a non-transferable-accountability reading. Their references to soundness and record keeping, reinforced by the express ensure wording in the ownership-record provision, also support substantive performance expectations. The packet does not settle whether any particular operational failure necessarily establishes breach or whether adequate conduct can suffice under an applicable standard.

Neither nominal retention of authority nor good outcomes alone conclusively establishes fulfilment. An applicable standard and facts about actual authority, supervision, operations and records remain necessary; the excerpts do not specify their sufficient combination.

Paragraph 14's punctuation supports an unconditional confirmation requirement and request-triggered demonstration. Footnote 5 can be harmonised as defining the minimum content of those acts while preserving that trigger, but its unqualified confirmation-and-demonstration wording supports a rival broader reading. The packet does not conclusively resolve the tension.

The SFC-satisfaction standard most directly attaches to demonstration in paragraph 14. Footnote 5 adds minimum compliance and smart-contract assurance content; whether high confidence qualifies only the smart-contract proposition or the whole minimum showing remains uncertain. Neither standard supplies a quantified threshold.

No request means paragraphs 15 and 16 do not themselves trigger obtaining an audit or verification or a legal opinion. It does not establish compliance, SFC satisfaction, or an exemption from substantive requirements. No actual request history is supplied.

The complete applicable text of 26EC22 paragraphs 10–13, missing footnote 2, relevant Appendix factors, actor definitions and application facts are needed to resolve remaining scope and sufficiency questions. No separate question or concern identity table was supplied.
